analysis.title: Tencent Rents 100,000 AI Chips At Huge Discount From Cash-Strapped Oracle In $7BN Deal
key_insights: FT reports Tencent signed its largest-ever overseas lease with Oracle: five years, multiple Oracle data centers in south-east Asia, roughly 100,000 advanced AI chips unavailable in China, estimated at about $7B with about 30% (~$2.1B) paid upfront. Neither company commented.

US export controls block sales of Nvidia's top chips to China but not rental in third countries. Tencent used the same route last December for ~15,000 Blackwell chips in Japan via Datasection (~$1.2B). Per the FT, Washington's efforts have made these leases pricier, with longer terms and bigger upfront payments.

Implied price is $14,000 per chip per year (~$1,170 a month), or about $1.60 per GPU-hour. Nebius on-demand prices cited: H100 $4.50, H200 $5.40, B200 $8.50, B300 $9.50. If Blackwell, Tencent pays about a quarter of the B200 rate. If Hopper, about 40% below the H100 index.

At the B200 index, 100,000 GPUs for five years is worth about $25B of compute against the $7B headline. The article offers three explanations: the $7B covers only part of the deal, the chips are older, or (judged most likely) Oracle is selling capacity at a steep discount to raise cash.

Oracle's past AI rental economics were thin: The Information reported in October 2025 that Oracle made about $900M of Nvidia rental revenue at roughly 14% gross margin and lost almost $100M renting Blackwells in one quarter. Five years of rent at $14,000 per GPU per year is about $70,000 per chip against Blackwell-class hardware cost estimated well over $40,000 per GPU.

Tencent's Q2 free cash flow was about -Rmb13.8bn ($2bn), its first negative quarter in over a decade, and capex rose 176% y/y to Rmb53bn ($7.9bn). The Oracle prepayment contributed. Goldman said Q2 capex was 47% above GSe and the stock fell 4.5%.

GS analyst Ronald Keung raised FY26/27/28 capex estimates by +39%/+49%/+42%, trimmed EPS, and cut his price target to HK$700 from HK$670 per the text, while staying Buy and 'encouraged by the aggressive spend'. Tencent management said AI is its 'highest capital allocation priority' and Q3 capex and prepayments will stay 'meaningful'.

Goldman's Sean Johnstone said the deal gives Tencent frontier compute without waiting on domestic silicon and supports Oracle's remaining capacity and backlog narrative (OpenAI, ByteDance, now Tencent). He flagged Oracle CDS reaction as the thing to watch.

Oracle fiscal Q1: RPO $664B, cloud infrastructure revenue +121%, over $30B of new AI contracts. Q1 capex $28.5B and free cash flow about -$5.4B. Management guided to up to $95B annual capex and a roughly $40B debt-and-equity raise. BofA models FY27 capex of $92.5B (+66%) with FCF margins bottoming around -50%/-38% in fiscal Q2/Q3, and customer prepayments covering only about 25% of capex.

Oracle credit stress: force majeure declared Sept 24-25 at Project Jupiter (2.25GW, New Mexico), 2056 bonds broke through 8% yield, about $30B of hardware capex in limbo. On Sept 28 Oracle CDS hit a record 251bps, hyperscaler CDS widened 2-4bps, and S&P rates Oracle BBB-, one notch above junk. ZeroHedge view: a downgrade to junk would push about $120B over the fallen-angel line.
SocGen counts Oracle's outstanding USD bonds at $117B versus $95B at end-2025. Hyperscaler bonds are up $143B in nine months, with about $200B of new USD issuance expected by year-end.

Paramount Skydance launched a $52B acquisition financing for Warner Bros. Discovery ($32B IG secured bonds, ~$12.4B high yield in the low-9% range, $7.5B term loan). The IG portion drew over $109B of orders. S&P cut Paramount to BB, and the combined company carries nearly $80B of debt at about 7x EBITDA. Close is slated for October 6.

Larry Ellison pledged another ~350M Oracle shares (~$9.2B) as loan collateral, bringing total pledged to about $57B, tying Oracle's largest shareholder's financing to Oracle's stock price. Paramount's 40-year paper competes for the same IG buyers as Oracle's 2056 bonds.
Goldman's ASEAN data center primer expects live capacity across six main hubs to grow from about 3GW to 13GW by 2030 (33% CAGR), with Johor about a third and power delivery the main bottleneck.

market_movers.rationale: S&P rates Oracle BBB-, one notch above junk. CDS at a record 251bps and 2056 bonds above 8% yield. The Tencent deal brings about $2.1B upfront but at a steep implied discount.
GS's Ronald Keung cut his price target to HK$700 after Q2 capex came in 47% above GSe and FCF turned negative, but kept Buy, encouraged by the AI spend.
S&P cut Paramount to BB, Moody's rates the first-lien notes junk, and the combined company carries nearly $80B of debt at about 7x EBITDA after the $52B Warner Bros. Discovery financing.

earnings_insights: Tencent Q2 (reported Aug 12): capex Rmb53bn ($7.9bn), +176% y/y and 47% above GSe. Free cash flow about -Rmb13.8bn ($2bn) versus about +Rmb43bn a year earlier. Stock fell 4.5% after the print.
Oracle fiscal Q1 (reported): RPO $664B, cloud infrastructure revenue +121%, capex $28.5B, free cash flow about -$5.4B. Management guided to up to $95B annual capex.
BofA pre-earnings estimate: Oracle FY27 capex $92.5B (+66%), FCF margin about -50% in fiscal Q2 and -38% in fiscal Q3.
Micron guided Q1 revenue to $61.5B (guidance, not a reported figure), cited as evidence memory prices are rising.
risk_factors: Oracle downgrade to junk from BBB- would push about $120B of debt into fallen-angel territory, per the author.
Oracle funding gap: up to $95B annual capex guided, a roughly $40B debt-and-equity raise, and prepayments covering about 25% of capex (BofA).
Project Jupiter force majeure leaves about $30B of hardware capex in limbo.
Ellison's pledged Oracle shares (~$57B in total) create a link between Oracle's stock price and his financing.
Hyperscaler bond supply of about $200B of new USD issuance expected by year-end (SocGen) against a rising-yield backdrop.
Power delivery is the main bottleneck for ASEAN data center growth (Goldman).
vol_and_positioning: Oracle CDS hit a record 251bps on Sept 28, and hyperscaler CDS widened 2-4bps. Goldman's desk flagged 'cracks in the credit space'.
geopolitical: US export controls block sale of Nvidia's top chips to China but not rental in third countries, so Chinese firms rent capacity in south-east Asia (Johor, Japan).
Washington's attempts to stop chip leakage via intermediate locations have made leases pricier, longer and more front-loaded, per the FT.

tension_points.bull_case: Oracle holds a $664B RPO backlog, +121% cloud infrastructure revenue, and over $30B of new AI contracts. The Tencent deal adds a customer and about $2.1B of upfront cash, supporting the backlog narrative (Goldman's Johnstone).
tension_points.bear_case: Oracle guides up to $95B annual capex and a roughly $40B raise. Prepayments cover only about 25% of capex (BofA). CDS is at a record, 2056 bonds yield over 8%, and the Tencent price implies a steep discount to market GPU rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An S&P downgrade of Oracle from BBB- to junk, which the author expects to push about $120B across the fallen-angel line. Oracle CDS reaction to the Tencent news is the near-term test.

theme_stances.key_argument: Oracle's capex needs and credit stress outweigh the benefit of the Tencent prepayment, which comes at a steep discount.
theme_stances.evidence: Downgrade to junk now not if but when

theme_stances.key_argument: Tencent is front-loading compute to lock in economics, and Goldman's Keung is encouraged by the aggressive spend.
